headline: Opinion: Sabres GM Kekalainen's Inaction On Hellebuyck Trade Has Proven Costly For Buffalo
take:
The Hockey News published an opinion piece arguing that Sabres GM Kekalainen's reported unwillingness to pay up for Connor Hellebuyck has proven costly for Buffalo. Hellebuyck now plays for New Jersey, a team that sits in the story only as his current club.

The numbers show a Buffalo team that looks more average than broken. The Sabres are 8-6-3 through 17 games, and their share of expected goals (the quality of chances each side creates) is 50%, an even split. Their goals minus expected goals is -6, so they have scored six fewer than their chances suggest, and their goalies have saved exactly what was expected, a goals saved above expected of 0. That points to a finishing problem more than a goaltending hole. Hellebuyck has a .913 save percentage and 1.46 goals saved above expected in five games so far this season, a small sample. Last year he saved 3.43 goals above expected over 57 games. The case that he would have lifted Buffalo is plausible, but the data doesn't show it as a gap yet.
